$description: Design system for joshuabriley.com, generated from design-system/tokens.json, design-system/rules.json, src/lib/component-catalogue.ts, and each component’s Props. Do not edit by hand: run `npm run design:context`. Human-readable version: /style-guide/.
workflow: Read tokens and rules (including rules.guidelines) before UI work.
Build from the listed components and token utilities; a new pattern is not part of the system until it appears in /style-guide/ and src/lib/component-catalogue.ts.
When an audit fails, fix the code. Adding tokens, exceptions, or baseline entries needs the site owner’s approval.

audits.checks: Hardcoded or off-palette colors, arbitrary values, literal font stacks, deprecated or forbidden prop values, token sync.
Live WCAG audit of /style-guide/ (needs the dev server).

tokens.$description: Editorial-Technical design tokens for joshuabriley.com, in W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) format. This file is the contract: src/styles/site.css (:root custom properties) and tailwind.config.mjs (theme.extend) implement it, and `npm run audit:design` fails if either drifts from it. A value that is not here is not part of the system. Extension keys under $extensions.site: cssVar = the custom property in site.css :root; tailwind = theme paths that must resolve to this token; deprecated/replaceWith = legacy aliases kept only so old markup renders; restrictedTo = the only files allowed to use the token.

paper.$description: Page background. Near-white with a faint cool cast.

raised.$description: Raised surfaces that lift off paper. Use sparingly: white cards on paper are the main sign that a page was generated rather than designed (see rules.json guidelines).

surface-warm.$description: Warm tint for small inline callouts only (e.g. the blog author card). Never a full-width section wash.

ink-soft.$description: Slightly lifted ink for layered dark surfaces.

ink-muted.$description: Secondary text. About 6:1 on paper, so it passes AA.

ink-faint.$description: Decoration only: separator dots, arrow glyphs, empty-state rings. At 2.8:1 it can't carry readable text at any size; use ink-muted for anything a reader has to read.

accent.$description: The single accent: deep denim navy on light surfaces (6.7:1). It follows the surface: site.css swaps --accent-rgb to accent-on-ink inside .bg-ink / [data-surface='dark']. Always reference it as `accent` / var(--accent), never as a literal, or it won't follow the surface.

accent-on-ink.$description: Accent value on dark ink surfaces (6.6:1). Applied automatically by the surface rules in site.css; you never select it directly.

accent-pressed.$description: Pressed / darker accent on light surfaces.

legacy.$description: Pre-rebrand Tailwind color names remapped onto the monochrome system so old markup still renders. Do not use them in new code; the audit fails on any new use.

sans.$description: Does almost all the work: body, UI, headings.

serif.$description: Display serif for character: headlines, oversized numerals, the editorial italic. Never small functional text. The CSS var keeps its historic name.

mono.$description: Technical and metadata moments: eyebrows, labels, code, indices.

script.$description: Signature wordmark only. One weight, no tabular figures, unreadable below about 20px.

ease-out.$description: Default easing for entrances and state changes.

hardcoded-token-color.why: A literal copy of a token value doesn't change when the token does, and a literal accent won't follow the surface onto ink.
hardcoded-token-color.fix: Use the token: a Tailwind class (text-ink, bg-paper, border-line, text-accent) or the custom property (var(--ink), rgb(var(--accent-rgb) / .2)). SVG presentation attributes can't take var(); use a class (fill-ink) or currentColor.

off-palette-color.why: Colors outside tokens.json are how second navies and warm near-blacks crept in.
off-palette-color.fix: Pick the nearest token. If the design really needs a new color, that is a design-system change: ask Josh, then add it to tokens.json, site.css and tailwind.config.mjs together.

default-palette-class.why: Tailwind's default palette (blue-500, gray-200, white, black) is still compiled because the config uses theme.extend, so these classes work but sit outside the system.
default-palette-class.fix: Use system colors: white → paper or raised, black → ink, gray-* → ink-muted / line, blue-* → accent.

legacy-color-class.why: Pre-rebrand names (navy, plum, coral, cream, sage, sky, charcoal, sunset, lemon) are aliases kept so old markup renders. New uses spread the confusion.
legacy-color-class.fix: Use the token named by replaceWith in tokens.json (navy/plum/charcoal → ink, coral → accent, cream → paper, sage/sky → ink-muted).

arbitrary-value.why: One-off Tailwind values (text-[0.6875rem], tracking-[-0.055em], rounded-[4px]) bypass the type scale and spacing that the primitives encode.
arbitrary-value.fix: Use the Heading / Text primitives or a standard Tailwind step (rounded-[4px] is just `rounded`). Arbitrary values belong only in the primitives listed in allowArbitraryValuesIn.

font-family.why: Font stacks are tokens. A literal family name skips the Astro font loader and its fallbacks.
font-family.fix: Use a font utility (font-sans, font-serif, font-mono) or var(--font-hanken) / var(--font-fraunces) / var(--font-geist-mono), or `inherit`.

restricted-font.why: The script face is the wordmark only (see restrictedTo in tokens.json).
restricted-font.fix: Use the Logo component; set any other text in font-sans or font-serif.

legacy-prop-value.why: Component props still accept pre-rebrand tone names for back-compat. They all map to the same few colors, which makes the intent unreadable.
legacy-prop-value.fix: Use the canonical value given in the message.

forbidden-prop-value.why: The prop value is valid TypeScript but a confirmed design decision rules it out.
forbidden-prop-value.fix: See the reason in the message.

token-sync.why: site.css and tailwind.config.mjs both implement tokens.json. If they disagree, the same token renders two ways depending on whether CSS or a utility class is used.
token-sync.fix: Change all three in one commit. Every Tailwind color/font key must map to a token, and every token's cssVar / tailwind value must match. Never baselined.

guidelines.rule: Social share (OG) cards are rendered only by src/pages/og-render/[slug].astro, never hand-made. Layout: copy column on the left (accent mono eyebrow with a short rule, Hanken 800 headline with the serif-italic wink and the accent period, then the header's script <Logo> plus the joshuabriley.com URL), and a full-height accent-tinted mat on the right holding real art from the site, tilted, large, and shadowed. The art is the page's own: a post's ArticleIllustration, a project's ProjectScreenshot teaser (with the tilt-shift blur off so it stays sharp), Josh's cut-out portrait (src/assets/og/portrait-cutout.png) for personal pages, or a fan of three for listings. Never the old 'JB' tile, and never a text-only card for a page that has art; text-only is for pages with nothing to show (legal, style guide). A new post or project gets its art automatically; for a new page, set `art` in src/lib/og-pages.mjs. Check the rendered PNG: drawing text must not be cut off by the card edge.
There is exactly one accent hue. Don't add a second highlight color, gradient, or 'candy' palette for variety; hierarchy comes from type weight, size and the serif italic.
Don't reach for bg-raised white cards with shadows to group content. Case studies use hairline columns and panels (border-line) on paper; the small Berxi-style testimonial is the model.
surface-warm appears only on small inline callouts, never as a Section tone or full-width wash.
Interactive islands must look like the site, not third-party widgets: navy accent plus in-key editorial hues, the site's type and controls.
Case-study artwork goes in a sibling <Container width="wide">, never inside .case-layout (the sticky rail paints over it). No nested scroll regions anywhere.
The homepage carries no 'Shipped at' client-logo or client-name band. Don't propose one.
ink-faint (text-ink-faint, Text tone="faint") is for glyphs and separators only, never words a reader has to read.
site.css owns global classes (.rule, .measure, .mono-label, …). Don't redefine them in a scoped <style>; scoped styles also don't reach DOM created at runtime, so pre-render and toggle instead.
/style-guide/ renders the system. A new pattern isn't part of the system until it appears there and in src/lib/component-catalogue.ts.

exceptions.reason: The demo palette is content: visitors swap accent hues to watch a token propagate.
Build-time generator for hand-drawn wireframe SVGs. Its colors and type are artwork, not interface.
Source sheets for case-study wireframe artwork, which depict client products in their own palette.
Overrides specific colors emitted by the Shiki code theme, so it has to match those literals.
